subject: Structured annual commit offer and pricing buckets for LogiHealth
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <procurement@logihealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: LogiHealth Legal <legal@logihealth.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual commitment options for API usage

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our execs want a simple, predictable pricing approach for 2027 that keeps per-token economics predictable while allowing us to scale. Can you send an outline of an annual commit structure across a Starter / Growth / Enterprise set of commits — rough token volumes, effective per-token discount bands, overage handling, and any flexibility (carryover, burst credits, outcome on downgrades)?

We'd like something we can review with Finance and Legal early next week. Also note security review will need a SOC2 summary but we'll request that separately.

Best,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Procurement, LogiHealth
Attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <procurement@logihealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exploring annual commitment options for API usage

Claire —

Appreciate the clear ask. Below is a concise starter proposal; I'm attaching a pricing matrix and a short SOW PDF for review. The numbers are purposely modular so we can tailor the Growth and Enterprise tiers to your expected monthly profile.

Overview (annual commit / recommended economics):
- Starter: 100M tokens/year (~8.3M tokens/month). Effective discount: 10% off list per-token. Overage: billed at list price + 10% (protects committed economics). No carryover.
- Growth: 500M tokens/year (~41.6M tokens/month). Effective discount: 20% off list. Overage: billed at list price (grace buffer up to 10% of committed monthly volume). Up to 25% of unused quarterly tokens can carry over within the following quarter.
- Enterprise: 2B tokens/year (~166M tokens/month). Effective discount: 30% off list. Overage: billed at 90% of list (i.e., discounted overage). Flexible carryover up to 50% of unused annual tokens, and burst credits included (3x monthly rate once per quarter for traffic spikes). Includes 99.9% latency SLA and priority onboarding.

Other commercial notes:
- Ramp schedule: We can front-load up to 25% of annual commit as refundable advance credit if you need upfront coverage.
- Audit & reporting: Monthly token usage report by model/route; quarterly bill reconciliation.
- Early termination / downgrade: Downgrade within first 6 months triggers a pro-rata true-up at list price; after 6 months, standard carryover rules apply.

Next steps: If this looks directionally right I'll loop in Marissa from our Billing team to prepare a clean SOW and a formal pricing matrix for Legal.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: LogiHealth_Pricing_Matrix_20260820.xlsx; Redwood_SOW_Annual_Commit_v1.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhou <procurement@logihealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exploring annual commitment options for API usage

Adding a few negotiation levers here from product/commercial ops that might help close faster:

1) Blended per-token floors: For Growth/Enterprise we can introduce a blended floor that ensures a minimum price for the first X tokens, then a deeper band thereafter. This helps when initial months are unpredictable.

2) Model family locking: If LogiHealth commits to a specified set of model families (e.g., rdx-chat-1 / rdx-embed-lite), we can apply an extra 3-5% discount to Growth/Enterprise tiers. This reduces surprise costs if you use very large models sporadically.

3) Governance credits: Offer a one-time operational credit (equivalent to 5% of the first-year commit) if you agree to a 12-month rolling usage review cadence and allow Redwood to use anonymized benchmark telemetry for joint performance tuning.

4) Procurement-friendly billing: Monthly invoices with cumulative quarterly reconciliation (rather than a single upfront invoice).

If procurement pushes back on carryover, we can replace it with a modest additive credit pool (non-refundable) that covers up to 10% of monthly overages. Happy to discuss trade-offs in a quick call.

— Jordan
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <procurement@logihealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Structured annual commit offer — LogiHealth (SOW + pricing)

Claire —

Thanks for reviewing the outline. Attached are: 1) a filled pricing matrix with exact per-token bands and net effective pricing by tier, and 2) a draft SOW that maps service levels and billing cadence. Highlights:
- Starter (100M): $0.000015/token effective; 10% discount; monthly invoicing; no carryover.
- Growth (500M): $0.000012/token effective; 20% discount; quarterly carryover up to 25%; blended floor option included (see sheet).
- Enterprise (2B): $0.0000105/token effective; 30% discount; 50% annual carryover; burst credits (3x monthly baseline once per quarter).

Redlines we expect from Legal: standard liability caps, data handling clause consistency, and SOC2 evidence delivery timing. We can accelerate SOC2 artifacts within two weeks of LOI.

Please review the attached and let me know two preferred times for a contract-review call next week. If you want, we can present the SOW to Finance and Legal together to speed approval.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SOW_Annual_Commit_v1.pdf; LogiHealth_Pricing_Matrix_20260820.xlsx
